title.narrative: Market study on the critical raw materials sector in Tanzania

description.narrative: The Tanzanian government, through its Critical and Strategic Minerals Strategy, has identified 25 critical and 18 strategic minerals that could significantly contribute to the growth of the country’s economy. Currently, the sector already (in)directly employs six million people. From the perspective of the Netherlands, being part of the European Union (EU) and its critical raw materials (CRMs) act, it is important to create diversified, sustainable and reliable supply chains of such CRMs, to support the transition that the EU is undergoing. Therefore, it is important to explore the possibilities to secure such supplies from Tanzania, to contribute to these goals. Not only to support societal transitions within the EU, but also through a commitment towards sustainability and value addition within the country of origin.The market study on the CRM sector in Tanzania and opportunities for Dutch value addition contains: 1. A description of the sector including its organisation, opportunities, challenges and development; 2. Identifies where Dutch companies and institutions can be of added value within the sector and its development, also on issues of circularity and sustainability; 3. Identifies concrete opportunities for off-take agreements of certain CRM’s to The Netherlands or the wider EU; 4. Contains a market access strategy for these companies and institutions, and how Dutch governmental institutions can assist in gaining that access; and 5. Identifies key players to be approached with the information obtained in the study to create business/institutional linkages.
